explanation: Map each distinct value to its inorder position. Consume preorder roots in order, recursively building the inorder slice to the left and then the slice to the right of each root.
timeComplexity: O(n) expected time for n nodes. The inorder map is built once, then each root is consumed once with expected constant-time position lookup.
spaceComplexity: O(n + h) auxiliary space for positions and recursion, plus the output tree. The position map stores n entries and recursion retains h interval frames; new nodes form the output.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C# implementation, reusing and refining the repository-authored Blind75 algorithm fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: The next preorder entry is the root of the current subtree. Its unique inorder position separates exactly the left-subtree keys from the right-subtree keys. Consuming those intervals recursively in preorder order therefore reconstructs the unique tree with the supplied distinct traversals.
walkthrough: Preorder [8,3,1,6,10,9] starts with root 8. Inorder splits there into [1,3,6] and [9,10]. The next roots 3 and 10 build children (1,6) and left child 9 respectively. Return [8,3,10,1,6,9].
edgeCases: Values are distinct and both traversals contain the same set.
Empty traversals reconstruct an empty tree.
A root at an inorder endpoint creates an empty child subtree.
